question.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{y}^{y+z}2x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le y\}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{y}^{y+z}2x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}[{x}^{2}]_{x=y}^{x=y+z}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(y+z)^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2yz+{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2yz+{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y}2yz+{z}^{2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[y{z}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{z}^{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{3}+\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{4}]}_{y=1}^{y=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(16-1) \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$
